name: Achensee
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Achensee is Tirol's largest lake—a magnificent fjord-like expanse cradled between the Karwendel and Rofan ranges, renowned for watersports and crystalline water.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Lake Achensee, lying at an elevation of 929 metres north of Jenbach in the Lower Inn Valley, reigns as Tirol's largest natural lake, stretching over nine kilometres in length with an area of 6.8 square kilometres and depths plunging to 133 metres. Often hailed as the 'Fjord of the Alps', the lake is dramatically flanked by the sheer limestone towers of the Karwendel mountains to the west and the crags of the Rofan range to the east. Boasting certified drinking-water purity and visibility extending up to ten metres below the surface, the lake captivates with iridescent shades spanning from turquoise to deep midnight blue. Cherished since the Habsburg emperors for royal angling and stag hunting, Achensee today represents an international haven for sailors, kitesurfers, wild swimmers, and alpine trail runners.

Route & Anforderungen

Outdoor recreation around Lake Achensee offers diverse routes suited to all abilities. A signature experience is the scenic lakeside trail tracing the craggy western shoreline from Pertisau to the historic Gaisalm—the only alpine pasture in Tirol accessible exclusively on foot or by passenger boat (walking time approx. 1.5 hours, requiring surefootedness on rocky singletrack). Families and leisure cyclists favor the broad, paved promenade between Maurach and Pertisau, which is completely level, barrier-free, and stroller-friendly. For the rocky Gaisalm trail, supportive hiking boots with rugged vibram soles are advised, while regular running shoes suffice for the paved southern lakeside promenade.

Besuch & Anreise

Approaching by car proceeds via motorway A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee) along mountain highway B181 directly to Maurach or Pertisau. Train passengers arrive at Jenbach mainline station, transferring either to the historical steam-driven Achenseebahn cog railway or to frequent regional electric buses. Well-organized municipal pay-and-display parking lots are situated throughout Pertisau, Maurach, and Achenkirch.

Tipps

Hike to the secluded Gaisalm pasture for a traditional alpine lunch and take the historical passenger steamboat back across the lake to Pertisau. Early mornings offer mirror-calm waters before thermal breezes kick up, creating world-class afternoon wind conditions for sailing and windsurfing.
preis: Free public access to shoreline paths and beaches
